paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) caused by heterozygous mutation in PKD1 or PKD2 usually begins in adulthood. Renal cystic disease is generally milder in PKD2 patients than in PKD1 patients (Losekoot et al., 2012). About 85% of ADPKD cases are caused by PKD1 mutations, and most of the rest are caused by PKD2 mutations. PKD1-linked families reach end-stage renal disease (ESRD) earlier than PKD2-linked families, at a mean age of 56 versus 70 years (Pei et al., 1998). Deltas (2001) noted that the clinical courses of PKD1- and PKD2-related disease cannot be told apart. However, PKD2 mutation carriers had a milder course, with average onset 10 to 20 years later and a lower probability of reaching end-stage renal failure.

paragraphs.text: Ravine et al. (1992) compared 5 ADPKD families (49 affected individuals) in which the PKD1 locus had been excluded with 18 PKD1-linked families (285 affected members). paragraphs.text: Wu et al. (2000) produced 2 mouse Pkd2 mutations: an unstable allele (WS25) that can undergo somatic rearrangement by homologous recombination to form a null allele, and a true null allele (WS183). Pkd2 -/- mice died in utero between embryonic day 13.5 and birth, with structural defects in cardiac septation and cysts in maturing nephrons and pancreatic ducts. Adult Pkd2 WS25/- mice developed kidney cysts, pancreatic ductal cysts, renal failure, and early death, with a median survival of 65 weeks compared with 94 weeks in controls. Adult Pkd2 +/- mice had no cystic disease or renal failure, but their survival fell between that of the other 2 groups. The authors took this as a first indication that Pkd2 haploinsufficiency harms long-term survival.

paragraphs.text: Pennekamp et al. (2002) found that mouse Pkd2 was ubiquitously expressed at headfold and early somite stages, with higher levels in the floorplate and notochord. They generated a Pkd2 knockout allele. In addition to previously described malformations, homozygous mutant embryos showed right pulmonary isomerism and randomization of embryonic turning, heart looping, and abdominal situs. In these embryos, Leftb and nodal were not expressed in the left lateral plate mesoderm (LPM), Ebaf was absent from the floorplate, and Pitx2 was expressed bilaterally in posterior LPM but was absent anteriorly. The embryonic midline was present, with normal Foxa2 and shh expression. The authors suggested that polycystin-2 acts downstream of or in parallel to shh and upstream of the nodal cascade.

paragraphs.text: Khonsari et al. (2013) found Pkd2 expression in craniofacial tissues. They used Wnt1Cre to delete Pkd2 conditionally in neural crest-derived cells in mice. The mutant mice had many signs of mechanical trauma, including fractured molar roots, distorted incisors, alveolar bone loss, and compressed temporomandibular joints, as well as abnormal skull shapes. None of these phenotypes was present at embryonic stages, when the head is under no significant mechanical stress in utero. The authors suggested that Pkd2 likely plays a critical role as a mechanoreceptor in craniofacial growth.
